newsitem.title: GERMANY: UPS CUTS US-EUROPE FLIGHTS, USES CHARTERS.
newsitem.headline: UPS CUTS US-EUROPE FLIGHTS, USES CHARTERS.

text.p: United Parcel Service said pilot action in support of the ongoing strike by UPS Teamsters employees has forced it to ground four aircraft in Europe and cancel two of its three daily transatlantic flights.
The company was still flying its Boeing 747 freighter service but had dropped two McDonnell Douglas DC-8F flights from its European hub at Cologne to Louisville, a UPS spokesman told Reuters.
The B747 transatlantic flight was being manned by a management crew since UPS International Pilots Association (IPA) members were taking sympathy action to support the strike, he added.
In addition two Boeing 727 freighters used to fly nightly Vienna-Nuremberg-Cologne and Zaragoza-Madrid-Cologne services were also not operating, he said.

But scheduled airlines had sub-chartered to operate these two routes and all other UPS flights within Europe were running normally since they were chartered aircraft flying in UPS colours but operated by other airlines.
UPS was loading shipments from other European countries on to direct scheduled airline flights to U.S .destinations to reduce volumes coming through Cologne.
The company was also putting parcels due for transport between Europe and Asia on direct flights of scheduled airlines to avoid using its reduced capacity via the U.S, he said.
"Our contingency plans are functioning well. We are not happy that the network we have built up is not working at present but the system is functioning at present," the spokesman added.
German shipments to the U.S. were at normal levels but imports from the U.S, to Germany, which made up only 10 percent of total business were down 50 percent because of the strike, he added.
Companies providing charter services for UPS include the German airline, WDL Aviation and Britain's Channel Express, he said. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
